$comment: A DENY LIST PREFIX-MATCHES A COMMAND STRING, SO IT CAN ONLY EVER BE AN ENUMERATION OF
SPELLINGS. The force-push entries below are the clearest case: they started as
`git push --force:*` and `git push -f:*`, were widened once to name every spelling that
targets `main`, and a security review of #80 then found four more --- `--force origin
HEAD:main`, `refs/heads/main`, a flag written AFTER the refspec, and any remote not called
`origin` or `upstream`. Those four are covered now. The next spelling nobody thought of is
not, and no amount of further widening changes that.
SO THE RULE IS MATCHED AS A PROPERTY WHERE THE FORMAT ALLOWS IT, AND THAT IS `hooks`.
`.claude/hooks/refuse-force-push-to-main.sh` parses the command and refuses any force-push
whose destination ref resolves to `main` --- in any spelling, on any remote, including one
behind `&&` or `;`, and including the bare forms that name no refspec at all and therefore
push whatever branch happens to be checked out. That is the rule stated once, rather than
its spellings listed many times.
BOTH ARE KEPT, LAYERED RATHER THAN DUPLICATED. The deny list refuses before the hook runs
and before a prompt is shown; the hook catches what an enumeration cannot reach. The hook
fails OPEN on its own internal error, deliberately --- a hook that failed closed on a bug
would block every push in the repository for a reason nobody could see --- and the deny
list is what is underneath it when that happens.
The hook has an adversarial self-test, `.claude/hooks/test-refuse-force-push-to-main.sh`,
with both halves: 17 commands that must be refused and 10 near-misses that must be
allowed. The allow half is the one that matters --- a hook that refused everything would
pass a refuse-only suite and make the repository unusable. Its first run found a real bug,
and the same one `tools/ci-local.py`'s preflight hit: plain `shlex.split` leaves `hi;` as
one token, so a force-push behind a semicolon was invisible.
Where a rule genuinely IS a spelling --- a literal path, an exact filename --- a list is
the right shape and this note does not apply to it.
